---
title: "Per-pair protein-property profiling of risk and nonrisk isoform pairs"
output: html_document
---

## Purpose

For every risk/nonrisk isoform pair this script asks which predicted protein property most
strongly distinguishes the two members of the pair. The isoform-level property table from
`03_protein_feature_annotation.Rmd` holds, for each pair, the risk-minus-nonrisk difference
of every property (Pfam domain content, intrinsic disorder, NetSurfP-3.0 relative solvent
accessibility and secondary structure, DeepLoc compartment probabilities, PTM counts,
AAindex residue indices, AlphaFold3 geometry). Because the properties live on incomparable
scales, each difference is divided by the standard deviation of that property across all
pairs, so that a scaled difference of 1 means "one SD of between-pair variation". Redundant
predictors of the same property (for example NetSurfP and AlphaFold3 estimates of coil
content) are collapsed to the strongest, properties are grouped into five families (fold and
disorder, localization, PTM, residue biochemistry, domain content), and the property with the
largest absolute scaled difference defines the pair's dominant change; pairs whose strongest
change is below 1 SD are classed as minimal/mixed. The same scaled differences are averaged
into oriented property axes for the heatmaps, and a per-pair sequence/structure similarity
table is derived from the AlphaFold3 pairwise alignment metrics.

## Manuscript outputs produced

- Methods, "Per-pair property profiling" (feature exclusion, 30 % missingness rule,
  SD scaling, ±3 cap, family grouping, 1-SD gate; 82 of 94 pairs with a dominant change).
- Fig. 4h (direction of the dominant property change) — drawn by
  `10_figure_and_table_generation.Rmd` from `per_pair_dominant_mode.csv`.
- Extended Data Fig. 5d (property-difference heatmap, 94 pairs) and Extended Data Fig. 7a
  (same heatmap for the 13 AP-MS bait pairs) — drawn by script 10 from the signature exports.
- Supplementary Table 16 (dominant mode, property axes and similarity per pair) — assembled
  by script 10 from `per_pair_dominant_mode.csv`, `pair_property_signatures_long.csv` and
  `pair_structure_vs_sequence_similarity.csv`.

## Inputs

- `OUT_PROPERTY_ISOFORM_WIDE` — isoform-level property table, one row per pair, written by
  script 03 (`<property>__delta`, `<property>__risk_value`, `<property>__nonrisk_value`).
- `OUT_PAIRS_UNIFIED_FLAGGED` — unified pair table with the `include_in_isoform_stats` flag
  (one pair per gene for genes with several pairs), written by script 02.
- `F_APMS_BAIT_PAIRS` — the 13 isoform pairs cloned as AP-MS baits (gene, risk PB, nonrisk PB).

## Outputs (all in `RES_06`)

- `per_pair_dominant_mode.csv` — dominant change mode per pair (script 10: Fig. 4h, Table S16).
- `pair_groupings_table.csv` — pair keys with mode, family and strength (script 10).
- `pair_property_signatures_long.csv` — oriented axis scores per pair (script 10: ED Fig. 5d,
  Table S16).
- `apms_pair_property_signatures_long.csv`, `apms_bait_pairs.csv` — the same scores for the
  13 AP-MS bait pairs, on the same scale (script 10: ED Fig. 7a).
- `property_axis_order.csv` — axis order and family for the heatmaps (script 10).
- `pair_structure_vs_sequence_similarity.csv` — per-pair sequence identity and TM-score
  (script 10: ED Fig. 5d, ED Fig. 7a, Table S16).
- `property_base_axis_map.csv`, `property_feature_sd.csv`, `property_feature_category.csv` —
  provenance tables documenting the axis mapping, the scaling denominators and the feature
  categories used.

## Run order

Requires `02_junction_isoform_mapping_and_pairs.Rmd` and `03_protein_feature_annotation.Rmd`.
Feeds `10_figure_and_table_generation.Rmd`.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
options(stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
```

```{r libraries}
source("config.R")
library(tidyverse)
set.seed(42)
ensure_dir(RES_06)
```

# 1. Parameters

The parameters below are the analysis choices stated in Methods ("Per-pair property
profiling"). They are defined once here so that every downstream step uses the same values.

```{r params}
# Only the risk - nonrisk difference columns ("__delta") enter the profiling; the raw per-side
# values are used solely to derive the similarity table.
FEATURE_REP <- "delta"

# Restrict to the pairs flagged include_in_isoform_stats (one pair per gene where a gene has
# several), giving the 94 sQTL-derived pairs plus the manual AP-MS pairs.
RESTRICT_TO_INCLUDED <- TRUE

# Methods: "features with more than 30 % missing values were dropped".
MAX_FEATURE_NA <- 0.30

# Methods: "features measuring global similarity, size or prediction confidence were
# excluded from profiling" -- they describe how different the isoforms are overall, not
# which property differs.
EXCLUDE_FEATURE_REGEX <- paste(c(
  "pct_identity", "tm_score", "query_coverage", "length_ratio",
  "n_gap_openings", "aligned_length",
  "aa_mw", "aa_length",
  "mean_plddt", "mean_pae", "nsp_mean_rsa",
  "total_gap_length"
), collapse = "|")

# Methods: "pairs whose strongest change was below 1 s.d. were classified as minimal/mixed".
GATE <- 1.0

pair_key <- c("gene_name", "pair_type", "risk_pb", "nonrisk_pb")
ID_COLS  <- c(pair_key, "cad_sqtl_junction")
```

# 2. Load the per-pair property table and the pair flags

The property table has one row per (pair, CAD sQTL junction); pairs with several junctions
are averaged to one row below. The flagged pair table supplies `include_in_isoform_stats`,
which keeps one pair per gene so that genes with several colocalized clusters do not count
more than once in the population statistics.

```{r load}
require_files(OUT_PROPERTY_ISOFORM_WIDE, OUT_PAIRS_UNIFIED_FLAGGED, F_APMS_BAIT_PAIRS)

iso_wide <- read_csv(OUT_PROPERTY_ISOFORM_WIDE, show_col_types = FALSE)

include_lookup <- NULL
if (RESTRICT_TO_INCLUDED) {
  flagged <- read_csv(OUT_PAIRS_UNIFIED_FLAGGED, show_col_types = FALSE)
  stopifnot(all(c("risk_pb", "nonrisk_pb", "include_in_isoform_stats") %in% names(flagged)))
  include_lookup <- flagged %>%
    group_by(risk_pb, nonrisk_pb) %>%
    summarise(include_in_isoform_stats = any(include_in_isoform_stats, na.rm = TRUE),
              .groups = "drop")
}
cat(sprintf("property table: %d rows x %d columns\n", nrow(iso_wide), ncol(iso_wide)))
```

# 3. Build the per-pair feature matrix

One row per pair and one column per property difference. Features are removed if they are
too sparse (the 30 % rule), have zero variance (no information to scale), or measure global
similarity, size or prediction confidence rather than a specific property.

```{r feature_matrix}
value_suffix <- "__delta$"

pick_features <- function(df) {
  feat_cols <- names(df)[str_detect(names(df), value_suffix)]
  feat_cols <- feat_cols[vapply(df[feat_cols], is.numeric, logical(1))]
  df %>% select(any_of(ID_COLS), all_of(feat_cols))
}
feat_mat <- pick_features(iso_wide)

# Collapse to one row per pair (a pair may be listed under more than one junction).
feat_cols_all <- setdiff(names(feat_mat), ID_COLS)
feat_mat <- feat_mat %>%
  group_by(across(any_of(pair_key))) %>%
  summarise(across(all_of(feat_cols_all), ~ mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE)), .groups = "drop")

if (!is.null(include_lookup)) {
  before <- nrow(feat_mat)
  feat_mat <- feat_mat %>%
    left_join(include_lookup, by = c("risk_pb", "nonrisk_pb")) %>%
    filter(is.na(include_in_isoform_stats) | include_in_isoform_stats) %>%
    select(-any_of("include_in_isoform_stats"))
  cat(sprintf("include_in_isoform_stats restriction: %d -> %d pairs\n", before, nrow(feat_mat)))
}

# Drop sparse features (> MAX_FEATURE_NA missing).
feat_cols <- setdiff(names(feat_mat), pair_key)
na_frac   <- vapply(feat_mat[feat_cols], function(x) mean(is.na(x) | is.nan(x)), numeric(1))
feat_cols <- setdiff(feat_cols, names(na_frac)[na_frac > MAX_FEATURE_NA])

# Drop zero-variance features (cannot be scaled).
var0 <- feat_cols[vapply(feat_mat[feat_cols],
                         function(x) { x <- x[is.finite(x)]; length(x) < 2 || sd(x) == 0 },
                         logical(1))]
feat_cols <- setdiff(feat_cols, var0)

# Drop similarity / size / confidence features.
feat_cols <- feat_cols[!str_detect(feat_cols, EXCLUDE_FEATURE_REGEX)]

cat(sprintf("feature matrix: %d pairs x %d property differences\n",
            nrow(feat_mat), length(feat_cols)))
```

# 4. Property categories, families and display names

Each feature is assigned to a category from its name, and categories are merged into the five
families used in the manuscript. Structure and disorder form one family because their
predictors are strongly collinear (a more disordered isoform is also less helical and more
solvent exposed), so counting them separately would double-weight a single change.

```{r property_categories}
categorize <- function(feat) {
  stem <- str_remove(feat, "__(delta|risk_value|nonrisk_value)$")
  dplyr::case_when(
    str_detect(stem, "helix|sheet|coil|rsa|plddt|radius_of_gyration|secondary") ~ "Structure",
    str_detect(stem, "idr|disorder")                                            ~ "Disorder",
    str_detect(stem, "pfam|domain")                                             ~ "Domains",
    str_detect(stem, "ptm")                                                     ~ "PTM",
    str_detect(stem, paste0("deeploc|membrane|signal|cytoplasm|nucleus|extracellular|",
                            "mitochond|^loc_|localiz|lysosome|peroxisome|golgi|^er_|plastid")) ~ "Localization",
    str_detect(stem, "tm_score|pct_identity|coverage|gap|length_ratio|aligned") ~ "StructSimilarity",
    str_detect(stem, "aa_length|^length|n_exons")                               ~ "Size",
    str_detect(stem, paste0("hydropath|polarity|volume|flexibility|grantham|kyte|zimmerman|",
                            "aa_hydro|aa_mw|aa_charge"))                        ~ "Biochemical",
    TRUE                                                                        ~ "Other"
  )
}
feat_category <- tibble(feature = feat_cols, category = categorize(feat_cols)) %>%
  # AlphaFold3 loop fraction is a secondary-structure measure; surface charge is a
  # biochemical property rather than a structural one.
  mutate(category = dplyr::case_when(
    str_detect(feature, "pct_loop")       ~ "Structure",
    str_detect(feature, "surface_charge") ~ "Biochemical",
    TRUE                                  ~ category))

family_of <- function(category) dplyr::case_when(
  category %in% c("Structure", "Disorder") ~ "Fold & disorder",
  category == "Localization"               ~ "Localization",
  category == "Biochemical"                ~ "Biochemistry",
  category == "Domains"                    ~ "Domains",
  category == "PTM"                        ~ "PTM",
  TRUE                                     ~ "Other"
)
feat_category <- feat_category %>% mutate(family = family_of(category))

# Readable property names for the exported tables.
pretty_prop <- c(
  nsp_pct_rsa  = "RSA (%)", nsp_mean_rsa = "RSA (mean)",
  nsp_pct_sheet = "β-sheet", nsp_pct_helix = "α-helix", nsp_pct_coil = "coil",
  idr_percent = "IDR%", idr_pct_disordered = "disorder",
  pfam_n_domains = "domain count", pfam_n_unique_domains = "unique domains",
  ptm_total = "PTM count", ptm_pct_exposed = "exposed PTMs",
  radius_of_gyration = "radius of gyration",
  hydropathy = "hydropathy", polarity = "polarity",
  volume = "volume", flexibility = "flexibility")
nice <- function(stem) {
  out <- ifelse(stem %in% names(pretty_prop), pretty_prop[stem],
                str_replace_all(str_remove(stem, "^(af3_|nsp_|deeploc_|iso_)"), "_", " "))
  unname(out)
}

# Methods: "redundant predictors of the same property were collapsed to the strongest".
# Features describing global divergence (alignment statistics) and the AlphaFold3 pTM
# fold-confidence score are excluded from the profiling at this stage.
PROFILE_EXCLUDE <- paste(c(
  "total_gap_length", "n_gap", "aligned_length", "pct_identity",
  "tm_score", "coverage", "length_ratio", "annot_overlap",
  "af3_iso_ptm$", "af3_ptm$"
), collapse = "|")

# Predictor-agnostic base property: af3_/af3_iso_/nsp_ variants of one property collapse to
# a single stem, and AlphaFold3 "loop" is unified with NetSurfP "coil".
base_stem_of <- function(stem) {
  b <- stringr::str_remove(stem, "^(af3_iso_|af3_|nsp_|iso_)")
  stringr::str_replace(b, "pct_loop", "pct_coil")
}

# One row per (pair, base property): the predictor variant with the largest |scaled delta|.
make_dedup <- function(pr) {
  pr %>%
    filter(is.finite(scaled_delta), !str_detect(stem, PROFILE_EXCLUDE)) %>%
    mutate(base = base_stem_of(stem), family = family_of(category)) %>%
    group_by(across(all_of(pair_key)), base) %>%
    slice_max(abs_scaled, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
    ungroup()
}

# Axis -> family lookup used when the signature axes are exported.
AXIS_FAMILY <- c(
  "Disorder/openness" = "Fold & disorder", "Domain content" = "Domains",
  "PTM load" = "PTM", "Hydrophobicity" = "Biochemistry",
  "Surface charge" = "Biochemistry", "Residue bulk" = "Biochemistry",
  "Loc: membrane" = "Localization", "Loc: secreted" = "Localization",
  "Loc: nucleus" = "Localization", "Loc: mitochondrion" = "Localization",
  "Loc: peroxisome" = "Localization", "Loc: ER" = "Localization")
```

# 5. Scaled property differences

Each risk-minus-nonrisk difference is divided by the standard deviation of that property
across all pairs, so that properties measured in different units become comparable; the sign
records whether the risk-associated isoform has the higher (positive) or lower (negative)
value. Properties are then ranked within each pair by absolute scaled difference, and the
collapsed table `dd` (one row per pair and base property) is the input to every later step.

```{r scaled_deltas}
# Scaling denominator: SD of each property difference across pairs.
delta_sd <- vapply(feat_mat[feat_cols], function(x) {
  x <- x[is.finite(x)]; if (length(x) < 2) NA_real_ else sd(x)
}, numeric(1))
delta_sd[!is.finite(delta_sd) | delta_sd == 0] <- NA

pair_long <- feat_mat %>%
  select(all_of(pair_key), all_of(feat_cols)) %>%
  pivot_longer(all_of(feat_cols), names_to = "feature", values_to = "delta") %>%
  mutate(
    stem         = str_remove(feature, "__delta$"),
    sd_feat      = delta_sd[feature],
    scaled_delta = delta / sd_feat,
    abs_scaled   = abs(scaled_delta),
    direction    = case_when(delta > 0 ~ "risk_higher",
                             delta < 0 ~ "risk_lower",
                             TRUE      ~ "no_change"),
    dir_sign     = case_when(delta > 0 ~  1L,
                             delta < 0 ~ -1L,
                             TRUE      ~  0L)) %>%
  left_join(feat_category, by = "feature") %>%
  filter(is.finite(scaled_delta))

pair_ranked <- pair_long %>%
  group_by(across(all_of(pair_key))) %>%
  arrange(desc(abs_scaled), .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(rank = row_number()) %>%
  ungroup()

dd <- make_dedup(pair_ranked)
# The dominant-mode call takes the second-ranked row per pair; duplicated rows would make
# that a copy of the first and collapse the clarity margin to zero.
stopifnot(!any(duplicated(dd[intersect(c(pair_key, "stem", "feature"), names(dd))])))
```

# 6. Oriented property axes

For the heatmaps, base properties are grouped into interpretable axes with a fixed orientation
so that a positive score always means the risk-associated isoform shifts toward the named pole
(more disordered/open, more domains, more PTMs, more hydrophobic, more positive surface, bulkier
residues, more of a compartment). Helix and sheet content, polarity and flexibility enter with
negative orientation because they move opposite to the axis they describe. Each axis score is
the mean oriented scaled difference of its member properties.

```{r signature_axes}
AXIS_MAP <- tibble::tribble(
  ~axis,                ~base_regex,                                 ~orient,
  "Disorder/openness",  "idr|disorder",                               1,
  "Disorder/openness",  "^pct_coil$",                                 1,
  "Disorder/openness",  "^pct_rsa$",                                  1,
  "Disorder/openness",  "radius_of_gyration",                         1,
  "Disorder/openness",  "^pct_helix$",                               -1,
  "Disorder/openness",  "^pct_sheet$",                               -1,
  "Domain content",     "^pfam_n_domains$|^pfam_n_unique_domains$",    1,
  "PTM load",           "^ptm_",                                      1,
  "Hydrophobicity",     "^hydropathy$",                               1,
  "Hydrophobicity",     "^polarity$",                                -1,
  "Surface charge",     "surface_charge",                             1,
  "Residue bulk",       "^volume$",                                   1,
  "Residue bulk",       "^flexibility$",                             -1,
  "Loc: membrane",      "cell_membrane",                              1,
  "Loc: secreted",      "extracellular",                              1,
  "Loc: nucleus",       "deeploc_nucleus",                            1,
  "Loc: mitochondrion", "mitochond",                                  1,
  "Loc: peroxisome",    "peroxisome",                                 1,
  "Loc: ER",            "endoplasmic|reticulum",                      1
)
AXIS_LEVELS <- unique(AXIS_MAP$axis)

# Each base property maps to the first matching axis; unmapped properties are not plotted.
base_axis <- bind_rows(lapply(unique(dd$base), function(b) {
  hit <- which(stringr::str_detect(b, AXIS_MAP$base_regex))
  if (length(hit)) tibble(base = b, axis = AXIS_MAP$axis[hit[1]], orient = AXIS_MAP$orient[hit[1]])
  else             tibble(base = b, axis = NA_character_, orient = NA_real_)
})) %>% filter(!is.na(axis))
cat(sprintf("%d base properties mapped to %d axes\n", nrow(base_axis), length(AXIS_LEVELS)))

# Per-pair oriented signature: mean(orient * scaled_delta) within each axis.
sig_long <- dd %>%
  inner_join(base_axis, by = "base") %>%
  mutate(oriented = orient * scaled_delta) %>%
  group_by(across(all_of(pair_key)), axis) %>%
  summarise(score = mean(oriented, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
```

# 7. Dominant change mode per pair

The dominant mode is the base property with the largest absolute scaled difference in the pair,
reported as an oriented axis (the mode map extends the heatmap axes to every DeepLoc
compartment) with its family and direction. A pair whose strongest change is below `GATE`
(1 SD) is classed as minimal/mixed, because no single property separates the two isoforms
more than the typical between-pair spread.

```{r dominant_change_mode}
MODE_MAP <- tibble::tribble(
  ~mode_axis,           ~base_regex,                                 ~orient,
  "Disorder/openness",  "idr|disorder",                               1,
  "Disorder/openness",  "^pct_coil$",                                 1,
  "Disorder/openness",  "^pct_rsa$",                                  1,
  "Disorder/openness",  "radius_of_gyration",                         1,
  "Disorder/openness",  "^pct_helix$",                               -1,
  "Disorder/openness",  "^pct_sheet$",                               -1,
  "Domain content",     "^pfam_n_domains$|^pfam_n_unique_domains$",    1,
  "PTM load",           "^ptm_",                                      1,
  "Hydrophobicity",     "^hydropathy$",                               1,
  "Hydrophobicity",     "^polarity$",                                -1,
  "Surface charge",     "surface_charge",                             1,
  "Residue bulk",       "^volume$",                                   1,
  "Residue bulk",       "^flexibility$",                             -1,
  "Loc: membrane",      "cell_membrane",                              1,
  "Loc: secreted",      "extracellular",                              1,
  "Loc: nucleus",       "deeploc_nucleus",                            1,
  "Loc: cytoplasm",     "cytoplasm",                                  1,
  "Loc: mitochondrion", "mitochond",                                  1,
  "Loc: peroxisome",    "peroxisome",                                 1,
  "Loc: ER",            "endoplasmic|reticulum",                      1,
  "Loc: Golgi",         "golgi",                                      1,
  "Loc: lysosome",      "lysosome",                                   1
)
MODE_PHRASE <- tibble::tribble(
  ~mode_axis,           ~up,                       ~down,
  "Disorder/openness",  "more disordered/exposed", "more ordered/compact",
  "Domain content",     "gains domains",           "loses domains",
  "PTM load",           "more PTMs",               "fewer PTMs",
  "Hydrophobicity",     "more hydrophobic",        "more polar",
  "Surface charge",     "more positive surface",   "more negative surface",
  "Residue bulk",       "bulkier/rigid",           "smaller/flexible",
  "Loc: membrane",      "more membrane",           "less membrane",
  "Loc: secreted",      "more secreted",           "less secreted",
  "Loc: nucleus",       "more nuclear",            "less nuclear",
  "Loc: cytoplasm",     "more cytoplasmic",        "less cytoplasmic",
  "Loc: mitochondrion", "more mitochondrial",      "less mitochondrial",
  "Loc: peroxisome",    "more peroxisomal",        "less peroxisomal",
  "Loc: ER",            "more ER",                 "less ER",
  "Loc: Golgi",         "more Golgi",              "less Golgi",
  "Loc: lysosome",      "more lysosomal",          "less lysosomal",
  "Other",              "higher (other property)", "lower (other property)"
)
mode_family_of <- function(ax) dplyr::case_when(
  str_detect(ax, "^Loc:")                                      ~ "Localization",
  ax == "Disorder/openness"                                    ~ "Fold & disorder",
  ax == "Domain content"                                       ~ "Domains",
  ax == "PTM load"                                             ~ "PTM",
  ax %in% c("Hydrophobicity", "Surface charge", "Residue bulk") ~ "Biochemistry",
  TRUE                                                         ~ "Other")
mode_phrase <- function(ax, ori) {
  i <- match(ax, MODE_PHRASE$mode_axis)
  ifelse(ori > 0, MODE_PHRASE$up[i], MODE_PHRASE$down[i])
}

# Base property -> first matching mode axis ("Other" if none).
base_mode <- bind_rows(lapply(unique(dd$base), function(b) {
  hit <- which(stringr::str_detect(b, MODE_MAP$base_regex))
  if (length(hit)) tibble(base = b, mode_axis = MODE_MAP$mode_axis[hit[1]], orient = MODE_MAP$orient[hit[1]])
  else             tibble(base = b, mode_axis = "Other", orient = 1)
}))

pair_modes <- dd %>%
  left_join(base_mode, by = "base") %>%
  mutate(oriented = orient * scaled_delta) %>%
  group_by(across(all_of(pair_key))) %>%
  arrange(desc(abs_scaled), .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  summarise(
    mode_axis       = dplyr::first(mode_axis),
    mode_oriented   = dplyr::first(oriented),
    mode_strength   = dplyr::first(abs_scaled),
    top_property    = nice(dplyr::first(stem)),
    second_axis     = dplyr::nth(mode_axis, 2),
    second_strength = dplyr::nth(abs_scaled, 2),
    .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(
    clarity     = mode_strength - dplyr::coalesce(second_strength, 0),
    gated       = mode_strength < GATE,
    mode_dir    = ifelse(mode_oriented > 0, "up", "down"),
    mode_sign   = ifelse(mode_oriented > 0, 1L, -1L),
    mode_family = ifelse(gated, "Minimal", mode_family_of(mode_axis)),
    mode_label  = ifelse(gated, "minimal / mixed change", mode_phrase(mode_axis, mode_oriented)),
    mode        = ifelse(gated, "Minimal / mixed", paste0(mode_axis, " ", mode_dir)),
    # Display variant with arrows, used only for figure labels.
    mode_display = ifelse(gated, "Minimal / mixed",
                          paste0(mode_axis, " ", ifelse(mode_oriented > 0, "↑", "↓"))))

# Keep the row order of the feature matrix.
pair_modes <- feat_mat %>% select(all_of(pair_key)) %>% left_join(pair_modes, by = pair_key)
write_excel_csv(pair_modes, OUT_PAIR_DOMINANT_MODE)

n_sqtl <- sum(pair_modes$pair_type != "manual_apms")
cat(sprintf("pairs: %d (%d sQTL-derived); with a dominant mode: %d; minimal/mixed: %d\n",
            nrow(pair_modes), n_sqtl,
            sum(!pair_modes$gated & pair_modes$pair_type != "manual_apms"),
            sum(pair_modes$gated  & pair_modes$pair_type != "manual_apms")))

# Compact grouping table (one row per pair) for the figure script.
grouping_tbl <- pair_modes %>%
  select(any_of(c(pair_key, "mode_family", "mode", "mode_dir", "mode_sign",
                  "mode_label", "top_property", "mode_strength", "clarity", "gated"))) %>%
  arrange(mode_family, mode, desc(mode_strength))
write_excel_csv(grouping_tbl, OUT_PAIR_GROUPINGS)
```

# 8. Sequence and structure similarity per pair

The AlphaFold3 pairwise alignment metrics (TM-score and percent identity between the risk and
nonrisk models) are excluded from the profiling but are reported alongside the heatmaps and in
Supplementary Table 16, because they show how different the two isoforms are overall. The
metrics may be stored in the per-side value columns or in the single `__delta` slot of the
property table, so the populated slot is selected at run time.

```{r similarity_table}
STRUCT_BASE <- "af3_pair_tm_score"      # structural similarity: TM-score, risk vs nonrisk model
SEQ_BASE    <- "af3_pair_pct_identity"  # sequence similarity: % identity over the alignment

num <- function(x) suppressWarnings(as.numeric(x))

# Report which of the candidate columns hold finite values for a metric.
slot_report <- function(base) {
  cand <- paste0(base, c("__risk_value", "__nonrisk_value", "__delta"))
  cand <- cand[cand %in% names(iso_wide)]
  tibble(column   = cand,
         n_finite = vapply(cand, function(c) sum(is.finite(num(iso_wide[[c]]))), integer(1)))
}

# Use the per-side columns when populated (averaging both perspectives), otherwise the
# best-populated single slot.
pick_pair_value <- function(base) {
  rep <- slot_report(base)
  rep <- rep[rep$n_finite > 0, , drop = FALSE]
  if (!nrow(rep)) stop("no finite values in any slot for ", base)
  persp <- rep$column[grepl("__risk_value|__nonrisk_value", rep$column)]
  use   <- if (length(persp)) persp else rep$column[which.max(rep$n_finite)]
  m <- vapply(use, function(c) num(iso_wide[[c]]), numeric(nrow(iso_wide)))
  if (is.null(dim(m))) m <- matrix(m, ncol = 1)
  list(value = rowMeans(m, na.rm = TRUE), used = use)
}

ps <- pick_pair_value(STRUCT_BASE)
pq <- pick_pair_value(SEQ_BASE)

sim_tbl <- iso_wide %>%
  mutate(.struct = ps$value,
         # seq_sim is a GLOBAL identity: identical residues over the longer isoform
         # (% identity x aligned length / max isoform length), so that a pair in which one
         # isoform is a truncation of the other scores low even if the aligned part matches.
         .seq = pq$value * num(af3_pair_aligned_length__delta) /
                pmax(num(aa_length__risk_value), num(aa_length__nonrisk_value)),
         .seq_local  = pq$value,                       # local identity over the alignment
         .len_ratio  = num(af3_pair_length_ratio__delta)) %>%
  group_by(across(all_of(pair_key))) %>%
  summarise(struct_sim    = mean(.struct,    na.rm = TRUE),
            seq_sim       = mean(.seq,       na.rm = TRUE),
            seq_sim_local = mean(.seq_local, na.rm = TRUE),
            length_ratio  = mean(.len_ratio, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ ifelse(is.nan(.), NA, .))) %>%
  filter(is.finite(struct_sim), is.finite(seq_sim))
write_csv(sim_tbl, OUT_PAIR_SIMILARITY)
cat(sprintf("similarity table: %d pairs\n", nrow(sim_tbl)))
```

# 9. Exports for the figure script

Two heatmaps are drawn downstream: Extended Data Fig. 5d for the 94 sQTL-derived pairs and
Extended Data Fig. 7a for the 13 AP-MS bait pairs. Seven of the 13 bait pairs are not in the
feature matrix, because their gene already contributes a systematically derived pair, so their
signature is computed here with the same scaling denominators (`delta_sd`), the same
deduplication and the same axis orientation; the two panels therefore sit on one scale.

```{r export_signatures}
# ---- the 13 AP-MS bait pairs ------------------------------------------------
bait <- read_csv(F_APMS_BAIT_PAIRS, show_col_types = FALSE)
names(bait) <- gsub("^﻿", "", names(bait))   # the header carries a byte-order mark
manual <- bait %>%
  transmute(gene_name  = .data[[grep("Gene", names(bait), value = TRUE)[1]]],
            risk_pb    = str_extract(risk, "PB\\.[0-9]+\\.[0-9]+"),
            nonrisk_pb = str_extract(.data[[grep("^non", names(bait),
                                                 ignore.case = TRUE, value = TRUE)[1]]],
                                     "PB\\.[0-9]+\\.[0-9]+")) %>%
  filter(!is.na(risk_pb), !is.na(nonrisk_pb))
cat(sprintf("AP-MS bait pairs: %d (%d already in the feature matrix)\n", nrow(manual),
            nrow(semi_join(feat_mat, manual, by = c("gene_name", "risk_pb", "nonrisk_pb")))))

# Signature for the bait pairs, scaled with the population delta_sd.
apms_feat <- iso_wide %>%
  semi_join(manual, by = c("gene_name", "risk_pb", "nonrisk_pb")) %>%
  select(any_of(pair_key), all_of(intersect(feat_cols, names(iso_wide)))) %>%
  group_by(across(any_of(pair_key))) %>%
  summarise(across(everything(), ~ mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE)), .groups = "drop")

apms_long <- apms_feat %>%
  pivot_longer(all_of(intersect(feat_cols, names(apms_feat))),
               names_to = "feature", values_to = "delta") %>%
  mutate(stem         = str_remove(feature, "__delta$"),
         sd_feat      = delta_sd[feature],
         scaled_delta = delta / sd_feat,
         abs_scaled   = abs(scaled_delta),
         direction    = case_when(delta > 0 ~ "risk_higher",
                                  delta < 0 ~ "risk_lower",
                                  TRUE      ~ "no_change"),
         dir_sign     = sign(delta)) %>%
  left_join(feat_category, by = "feature") %>%
  filter(is.finite(scaled_delta)) %>%
  group_by(across(all_of(pair_key))) %>%
  arrange(desc(abs_scaled), .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(rank = row_number()) %>%
  ungroup()

apms_dd  <- make_dedup(apms_long)
apms_sig <- apms_dd %>%
  inner_join(base_axis, by = "base") %>%
  mutate(oriented = orient * scaled_delta) %>%
  group_by(across(all_of(pair_key)), axis) %>%
  summarise(score = mean(oriented, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(axis = factor(axis, levels = AXIS_LEVELS))
missed <- manual %>% anti_join(apms_sig, by = c("gene_name", "risk_pb", "nonrisk_pb"))
if (nrow(missed)) warning(sprintf("%d bait pair(s) without a signature", nrow(missed)))
write_excel_csv(apms_sig, OUT_APMS_PAIR_SIGNATURES)
write_excel_csv(manual,   OUT_APMS_BAIT_PAIRS)

# ---- the sQTL-derived pairs ---------------------------------------------------
sqtl_sig <- sig_long %>%
  left_join(pair_modes %>% select(all_of(pair_key), mode_family, mode_strength,
                                  mode_axis, mode_oriented, gated),
            by = pair_key) %>%
  mutate(axis = factor(axis, levels = AXIS_LEVELS))
write_excel_csv(sqtl_sig, OUT_PAIR_SIGNATURES_LONG)

# ---- lookups and provenance tables -------------------------------------------
write_excel_csv(tibble(axis = AXIS_LEVELS, family = unname(AXIS_FAMILY[AXIS_LEVELS])),
                OUT_PROPERTY_AXIS_ORDER)
write_excel_csv(base_axis,     file.path(RES_06, "property_base_axis_map.csv"))
write_excel_csv(tibble(feature = names(delta_sd), sd = unname(delta_sd)),
                file.path(RES_06, "property_feature_sd.csv"))
write_excel_csv(feat_category, file.path(RES_06, "property_feature_category.csv"))

cat(sprintf("exported %d pair x axis rows (sQTL pairs) and %d (AP-MS pairs)\n",
            nrow(sqtl_sig), nrow(apms_sig)))
```
